source.title: Panel discussion: 5 years of JMAP - experiences and outlook
source.preparation: Original excerpts re-encoded to 640px H.264/AAC for reliable decoding; 3 seconds of trailing silence added. No generated or replaced speech.

method.capture: Native getDisplayMedia tab audio; automatically selects only the named test video tab
method.provider: Actual deployed Azure Speech, Azure AI Search and Azure OpenAI
method.authentication: Genuine delegated operator token and actual one-use API tickets; temporary grants removed
method.qualityAssessment: Manual review of actual transcript and generated replies; not an automated semantic-quality score

timingDefinition.firstReply: Receipt of last final transcript to receipt of first nonempty delta for its completed response

cases.actualReply: Which details would be most useful for this discussion?
cases.review: The introduction request was recognized. The corrected policy asked for clarification instead of fabricating the user's project or personal experience. A personalized introduction still requires verified user facts.

cases.actualReply: Could you clarify whether you want the main theoretical benefits of JMAP, or a comparison with other mail protocols?
cases.review: The JMAP adoption-benefit question was recognized, but the final response was more cautious than needed: it asked for clarification rather than directly answering. A noncritical phrase was mistranscribed as 'trust round'.

cases.actualReply: The main benefit is faster, simpler sync, because you can get all the information in fewer calls and batch email retrieval. If you want, I can also explain the benefit in a more general way.
cases.review: Context survived a real speaker change and the reply reflected faster synchronization and fewer calls. Some specialized protocol names were garbled; no numerical word-error rate is claimed.

priorFailuresRetained: Windows automation crashed or stalled; these attempts were not counted as passes.
The initial 160ms audio worklet pool stopped under short UI stalls. It was replaced by a bounded one-second pool with explicit overflow and regression tests.
A later Windows run exceeded the separate one-second network upload bound during a long stall. The final isolated Linux run does not prove that every Windows/environment stall is resolved.
Earlier introduction responses invented a project and personal history. Policy changes were tested against real Azure responses and the same recorded question.
limitations: Three selected excerpts totaling 88 seconds are not a long-meeting soak test.
No human-aligned ground-truth transcript was available; published automatic captions contain errors and were not treated as authoritative.
No live Teams call, interactive tenant login or manual chooser clicking was verified.
Technical-term transcription and directly useful answers still require broader evaluation.
No private work knowledge was uploaded; irrelevant synthetic knowledge returned no accepted sources.
